The Gutaifan gelding ran well on his return from a little break when chasing home easy winner Are You In Or Out at Fairyhouse just over three weeks ago. Although he arguably didn't have much to beat at the northern venue, the Joseph O'Brien-trained colt landed short odds in impressive fashion. selections.comment: Having caught the eye staying on late on her first run beyond a mile last time, AMAVASYA has to be of interest over further still. The Michael Grassick-trained filly also has the advantage of racing against her own age group here, after picking up valuable handicap experience against her elders in that aforementioned Leopardstown race. Bred to appreciate a test of stamina, the daughter of Sea The Moon has strong claims despite her wide draw. Whats New has shaped with promise on a couple of occasions since switching to handicaps. Perhaps, the application of a first-time visor can bring about further improvement. Lisnadill should be involved having suffered an interrupted passage when third at Gowran recently.

Placed on his first four starts, the Aidan O'Brien-trained colt easily landed a maiden at Gowran Park on his penultimate start. While the step into Group 1 company proved a bridge too far last time, the son of Wootton Bassett remains capable of making his presence felt in black type races. He should take this prize before his sights are raised once again. A beaten favourite at Cork last time, Storm Piece is almost certainly capable of better. Ger Lyons' colt had impressed when winning his maiden prior to that. The unexposed Fingerpaint is not one to dismiss lightly.

selections.comment: CIRCLE OF MAGIC made an encouraging debut over 6.5f last month when fourth in a decent novice and the form of that race has been franked since with the second and third both going on to score next time. Archie Watson's colt sets the standard and can raise the bar higher to open his account. The only winner in the field, Strength Of Spirit, won a seller last time and while that was an improved effort it's still a bit below the level set by the selection. He's a threat but Vincenzo Peruggia is feared more. He too made a promising start to his career when a close up third in a novice at Hamilton, where the second then went on to open his account next time. He has to prove his stamina for this 7f having flattened out over 6f on debut but shouldn't be too far away if his stamina holds. Both newcomers hail from powerful yards and need respecting. A market move for either should be taken seriously

selections.comment: It's pretty tight between Mo Of Cairo, Mission Classified and Come On Over on what they've achieved in their two runs each to date. Of the trio, the former is marginally preferred given the volume of support he's attracted on both starts and Kevin Ryan's colt can build on his latest effort where he flattened out late over 6f now dropped back to this 5f. However, AMBISHIO, who has a bit to make up on the trio above on his sole run, could be undervalued in the market and can take a significant step forward to possibly take top honours. He was only fourth beaten four lengths in a maiden at Nottingham on debut but the form of that looks a lot brighter since the winner that day ran a screamer at Royal Ascot to be a fine fourth of 15 in the G2 Norfolk Stakes. Micheal Appleby's colt could represent a bit of each way value. Missiion Classified is just preferred to Come On Over to fill the frame

selections.comment: The two key protogonists on paper, CANDLEFORD and Teumessias Fox, both have questions to answer after their respective Royal Ascot appearences but both can be excused somewhat. Candleford was making his season debut and never got into the race when last of 12 in the G2 Hardwicke Stakes. Last season he ran just twice, winning a Listed event and was then a good fourth in the 2024 Hardwicke Stakes. A return to anything like that level would suffice. Teumessias Fox is not far behind the selection on official ratings (4lb) and was in top form before struggling in the Duke Of Edinburgh Stakes handicap at Ascot. He can bounce back and give the selection most to do. Karmology needs to take a step forward to challenge the aforementioned but is very dependable and is poised to exploit any shortcomings if the pair don't return to somewhere near their best

She looked well ahead of the handicapper when landing a class 4 handicap at Sandown last time and can cope with 5lb rise. selections.comment: A weak affair where few can be trusted to deliver their best and those in form don't set an inspiring standard. Toota is tempting as one of a very few that can be trusted (up to a point) to run her race and give something like best but she'll likely to find a few too good. DOLLY'S DELIGHT could be the solution having improved markedly on a poor season opener to grab a place at Doncaster last time beaten a little over a length. That was just her sixth run and she can build on that and hopefully open her account. Almutraf, the only last timne out winner in the field, is a big threat given that win came off the back of a near six month break and he has fair scope for improvement on just his sixth run. He should go close if transferring his ability to the turf (his debut run came on deep ground, his only go on turf). Mavetheforcebewivu is interesting having belied huge odds of 125/1 to land a place last time and may be able to build on that now rediscovering some form. However, she's been seriously inconsistent so far in her career and is a risky proposition at much shorter odds. That said, if running her race she'll be bang there

He has been in excellent form of late and remains thrown in on his best efforts. A stiff track will play to his strengths as will the soft ground and he can defy top weight. Of the others Sacred Falls looks best treated but she needs to prove her effectiveness on the easier surface.

A Mere Bagatelle was poor on his last run but was in good form in both codes in Ireland prior to that and starts out for a new stable off a generous mark. He is strongly resepected given his yard's fine record with his new recruits and could chase the selection home ahead of Achnamara. That rival was let down by a slow start here last time but his pair of winter hurdles victories suggest he is capable of better.

Consistent bottom weight Blufferonthebus is also respected after taking a good race on easy ground here last time.

He can make amends here at the expense of veteran Ravenscraig Castle who posted a fine effort on his flat return at a stiff venue. He's well treated on his form in both codes and should be thereabouts despite a poor strike rate. Of those at bigger prices veteran hurdler Ashington is given a small chance as he's well treated on his form in that sphere but will need a stiff test at the trip.

She is 3 from 4 now with connections seeking Group 1 glory in the Nassau Stakes at Goodwood later this month will be expected to win what looks a 2-horse race here. Recent Wathnan purchase Scenic is next best, she does have experience on her side and is a Group 3 winner herself winning the Bronte Cup Fillies' Stakes last time out, no issues down in trip but will need to be firing to put it up to the favourite.

selections.comment: Not the strongest race on paper by any means, but it might pay for a yard that clearly knows how to land the race with Dave Evans and his runner DAVVY. The yard has won 2 of the last 9 runnings of this contest, and their runner here has plenty of experience under his belt and is also a previous winner, which is a fair bit more form than most of the rest have shown. He didn't stay the 7 furlongs last time out, so draw a line through that; back down in trip, he looks a sure-fire thing to run well in this and land the prize. Mare Of London has been getting slightly better with each run; if she can replicate the 3rd place finish from her second-ever start, then she will no doubt go well here. And Gullane Girl was a decent enough 4th on debut; she can progress here and fill the places.

selections.comment: NARDRA was sent off on 11/4 for Group 3. Nell Gwyn Stakes over 7 furlongs, now stepping back down to this 6-furlong trip, which she won over on her debut effort at Haydock last season, she will be pretty hard to beat here. She was pretty exceptional on debut, and the fact she was well fancied for a Group 3 contest on her seasonal debut would suggest they feel she is a pretty talented animal. She will be hard to stop here in what is a very winnable contest. Strobelight hails from a decent yard that does well with their youngsters on debut; however, she might be chasing for places here given the fact we have a talented favourite in this. And Knight Of India comes from a yard going well at present; she is well bred and could run well to fill the places here.

And Offiah's Boy could back up last time's run and fill the places here.

He is now 8 lb higher than his last winning mark and is actually running off a career-high mark; however, Connor Planas takes off a valuable 3 lb for the apprentice allowance, which offsets the burden from his last raise in the weights. The yard is going well at present, and he could be hard to stop here. Gundogan has been running well for his new yard, a 3rd on his penultimate start before coming 2nd last time out; he might have to unfortunately settle for another 2nd place effort here. Panelli is very lightly raced and could be anything; he could put in another solid effort here and place.

Roscioli is another one who arrives into this off the back of a good 2nd last time, and he can fill the places here.

Prior to that he was a winner over C&D and could add to that here on favourable quick ground.

All of his best efforts have come at Navan suggesting that this similar venue will suit and he could surprise at generous odds. Maiden Jackandthefox has been in good form on the AW and turf since being dropped to sprint trips and can complete the places.
